title: Longest stretch without repeated characters
prompt: Return the maximum length of a contiguous substring with no repeated characters. Treat uppercase and lowercase as distinct.
hints: The candidate substring changes as the right pointer advances.
If a repeated character is inside the current window, move its left boundary.

title: Shortest log fragment containing required tokens
prompt: Return the shortest substring of text containing all characters of required, respecting their multiplicities. Break ties by earliest starting position. Return "" if impossible or required is empty.
hints: A candidate window must satisfy character counts, not just membership.
Expand until valid, then shrink while it remains valid.

title: Count consecutive batches matching a net total
prompt: Return the number of nonempty contiguous subarrays whose sum equals target. Values can be negative or zero, so a standard nonnegative sliding window is not sufficient.
hints: Subtract two prefix sums to obtain the sum between them.
Count how often the required earlier prefix has appeared.

title: Longest request window with at most k services
prompt: Return the longest contiguous substring containing at most k distinct characters. Return zero for k=0 or an empty string.
hints: Track frequencies of symbols currently in the window.
Shrink only when the number of distinct symbols crosses the limit.

title: Consolidate closed maintenance windows
prompt: Merge intervals [start,end] into disjoint closed intervals, sorted by start. Intervals share time when one endpoint equals another, so touching intervals must merge. Do not mutate the input.
hints: Sort by the starting point.
The previous merged interval is enough to decide whether to extend it.

title: Insert a maintenance window into a schedule
prompt: Existing intervals are sorted, pairwise disjoint, closed [start,end] intervals. Insert new_interval, merge any overlapping or touching intervals, and return the updated sorted schedule.
constraints: 0 <= len(intervals) <= 100000; start <= end; original intervals are disjoint and do not touch.
hints: Walk through intervals before, during and after the insertion.
Merge while their starts are at or before the current new end.

title: Minimum concurrent worker slots
prompt: Each job occupies a half-open time interval [start,end). Return the minimum number of workers needed to run all jobs without overlap. A worker ending at t can start another job at t.
hints: Only the earliest finishing active job affects reuse next.
A min heap holds end times of jobs that are still active.

title: Kth largest distinct response size
prompt: Return the kth largest distinct integer in nums, not the kth largest element counting duplicates. k is valid.
constraints: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; 1 <= k <= number of distinct values.
hints: Remove duplicate values before ranking.
A size-k min heap keeps only the k best candidates.

title: Next higher daily latency
prompt: For each day i return the number of days until a strictly higher latency occurs. Return zero if no later day is higher. Equal latencies do not count.
hints: Some earlier indices are still waiting for a better later value.
Keep unresolved indices in a monotonically decreasing stack.

title: Locate a target in rotated configuration IDs
prompt: nums is a strictly increasing integer array rotated at an unknown pivot. Return the index of target, or -1 if missing. Do not scan linearly.
hints: One half of any rotated-sorted search range is sorted.
Determine whether the target belongs in the sorted half.

title: Find the smallest value in a rotated array
prompt: A strictly increasing list was rotated some number of positions. Return its smallest value in logarithmic time. The input is nonempty and has no duplicates.
hints: Compare the midpoint to a known endpoint.
The minimum lies in the unsorted side, including a boundary that may be the pivot.

title: Implement an LRU response cache
prompt: Process operations ["put", key, value] and ["get", key] on a cache of capacity slots. Return the list of results from get operations only (value or -1 when missing). Both a successful get and a put of an existing key make that key most recently used. Capacity may be zero.
hints: Which end of your ordering should represent the least recently accessed key?
A lookup and an update must both refresh recency, then evict if necessary.

title: Validate a search tree from an array
prompt: A tree is represented as a binary heap-style array: root at 0, children of index i at 2*i+1 and 2*i+2; null denotes absent nodes, and descendants of null nodes are ignored. Return whether all reachable nodes satisfy strict BST ordering (no duplicates). An empty tree is valid.
constraints: 0 <= len(tree) <= 100000; values are integers or null.
hints: The restriction on a node comes from all its ancestors.
Pass lower and upper bounds as you traverse.

title: Return tree nodes by depth
prompt: A tree uses heap-style indexes (left=2*i+1, right=2*i+2), with null for absent nodes. Ignore descendants of missing nodes. Return values grouped by depth, left to right. Return [] when root is missing.
constraints: 0 <= len(tree) <= 100000; values are integers or null.
hints: The desired groups correspond to the order of a queue traversal.
Carry the depth with each enqueued index.

title: Lowest shared manager in a BST
prompt: The input tree uses heap-style indexing, is a valid BST with distinct integer values, and contains p and q. Return the value of their lowest common ancestor. A node can be an ancestor of itself.
hints: In a BST, values smaller than a node are to its left.
Find the first node where the two values split into different directions.

title: Detect a loop in a linked chain
prompt: Represent a singly linked structure as next_index, where next_index[i] is a valid next index or -1 for null. Starting at start (-1 means empty), return True if following links ever repeats a node; otherwise False. Do not modify the array.
constraints: 0 <= len(next_index) <= 100000; start is -1 or a valid index.
hints: A linked chain can be explored without extra visited memory.
If two pointers advance at different speeds, they eventually meet inside a cycle.
